(Phoenix, Arizona) | college = [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] (2020–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 18 | draft_team = [[Chicago Bulls]] | career_start = 2022 | years1 = {{nbay|2022|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Chicago Bulls]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]]–[[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = →[[Windy City Bulls]] | years3 = {{nbay|2025|end}} | team3 = [[Philadelphia 76ers]] | years4 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team4 = →[[Delaware Blue Coats]] | years5 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team5 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | highlights = * [[Pac-12]] All-Defensive Team (2022) }} '''Dalen Lee Terry''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|d|eɪ|l|ən}} {{respell|DAY|lən}};{{cite press release |author= |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 17, 2024}} born July 12, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]], and was drafted with the 18th overall pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. As a sophomore in 2022, Terry was named to the [[Pac-12]] All-Defensive Team. ==High school career== Terry is a native of [[Phoenix, Arizona]], and attended [[Corona del Sol High School]] in [[Tempe, Arizona]], where he played with teammates [[Alex Barcello]] and [[Saben Lee]] before transferring to Hillcrest Prep in Phoenix. In two years at Hillcrest, Terry averaged 15.8 points, 7.4 rebounds, 10.3 assists, 3.7 steals and 1.9 blocks per game.{{cite web |title=Dalen Terry's Basketball Stats |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/dalen-terry/Tj7HgNIjEeiAxKkkK9HIDg/basketball/stats.htm |website=maxpreps.com}} He played his [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball for the Compton Magic with other [[Pac-12]] players such as [[Johnny Juzang]], [[Isaiah Mobley]], [[Evan Mobley]] and [[Onyeka Okongwu]]. ===Recruiting=== Terry was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] in the 2020 class and the No. 46 overall player, according to [[247Sports]]. On July 23, 2019, he committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], being the first commit in the 2020 class for Arizona.{{cite web |title=2020 4-star wing Dalen Terry commits to Arizona |url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2019/7/23/20707998/dalen-terry-commits-arizona-wildcats-basketball-recruiting-2020-class-rankings-highlights-scouting |last=Kelapire |first=Ryan |date=July 23, 2019 |accessdate=May 2, 2023 |website=azdesertswarm.com }} Terry had offers from [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]], [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]] and [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]], among others. He was joined in the 2020 recruiting class by [[Bennedict Mathurin]], [[Ąžuolas Tubelis]] and [[Kerr Kriisa]] among others to give Arizona the Number 7 overall recruiting class for 2020.{{cite web |title=Arizona 2020 Basketball Commits (7) |url=https://247sports.com/college/arizona/Season/2020-Basketball/Commits/ |website=[[247Sports.com]]}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Dalen Terry | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Phoenix, AZ]] | highschool = Hillcrest Prep (AZ) | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 190 | 40 = | commitdate = July 23, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 84 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = Arizona 2020 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2020 Arizona Wildcats Recruiting Class | rivals school = arizona | scout s = | espn schoolid = 12 | 247 overall = 46 | rivals overall = 51 | espn overall = 63 | accessdate = September 5, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== As a freshman at Arizona, Terry appeared in all 26 games for the Wildcats, starting 14 of them while averaging 4.6 points, 3.2 rebounds, 1.5 assists per game.{{cite web |title=CAREER HIGHLIGHTS |url=https://arizonawildcats.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/dalen-terry/12919 |website=arizonawildcats.com }} His highest point total came against in-state rival [[2020–21 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]], scoring 13 points, while shooting 3-of-3 from three-point range. Arizona would be placed on self-imposed post season ban, thus Terry would not play in the [[2021 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|2021 Pac-12 tournament]] or the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021 NCAA tournament]]. In his sophomore season, Terry started all 37 games for the Wildcats, in which he averaged eight points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 steals per game. He finished second in the Pac-12 in assist-to-turnover ratio (2.84), sixth in assists per game (3.92), eighth in field goal percentage (50.2) and ninth in steals per game (1.24). He became one of the marquee defensive players in the conference earning him All-Defensive First Team. Terry helped Arizona to a 33–4 record, winning the 2021 [[Roman Main Event]], [[2021–22 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 Conference regular season]] and [[2022 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|2022 Pac-12 tournament]] titles. Arizona returned to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]] for the first time since 2018. Terry scored a career-high 17 points in his final game as a Wildcat against [[2021–22 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]].{{Cite web |date=2022-03-24 |title=Arizona's Season Comes to an End in the Sweet 16 |url=https://arizonawildcats.com/news/2022/3/24/mens-basketball-arizonas-season-comes-to-an-end-in-the-sweet-16.aspx |access-date=2024-11-10 |website=University of Arizona Athletics |language=en}} On April 22, 2022, he declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility. He later decided to remain in the draft.{{cite web |title=Arizona guard, potential first-rounder Dalen Terry to remain in NBA Draft |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3490556/2022/05/31/arizona-guard-potential-first-rounder-dalen-terry-to-remain-in-nba-draft/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=May 2, 2023 |date= June 1, 2022 |last=The Athletic Staff}} == Professional career == ===Chicago Bulls (2022–2026)=== Terry was selected by the [[Chicago Bulls]] with the 18th overall pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{cite web | Bulls.{{Cite web |title=Bulls Sign Dalen Terry To Rookie Scale Contract |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/07/bulls-sign-dalen-terry-to-rookie-scale-contract.html |date=July 8, 2022 appearances (including two starts) for the Bulls in the [[2023–24 NBA season]], logging averages of 3.1 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 1.4 assists.{{Cite web|title=Dalen Terry 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4433159/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=April 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} He played in 73 games (starting five) for Chicago during the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]], averaging 4.5 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 1.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Dalen Terry 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4433159/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=April 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Terry made 34 appearances for the Bulls in the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], compiling averages of 3.5 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 1.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Dalen Terry 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4433159/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=April 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2026)=== On February 5, 2026, Terry was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Guerschon Yabusele]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chicago-bulls-acquire-guerschon-yabusele|title=CHICAGO BULLS ACQUIRE GUERSCHON YABUSELE|work=NBA.com|date=February 5, 2026}} Later, on the same day, Terry was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for [[Jose Alvarado (basketball)|Jose Alvarado]].{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Pelicans complete trade with New York Knicks |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-nba-trade-deadline-new-york-knicks-jose-alvarado-february-5-2026 two-way contract.{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Dalen Terry To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-sign-dalen-terry-to-two-way-contract|access-date=February 10, 2026|website=sixers.com}} On April 10, the 76ers signed him to a two–year, standard NBA contract worth $2.7 million.{{Cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Announce Roster Moves|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-sign-dalen-terry|access-date=April 24, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} Terry made 14 total appearances for Philadelphia, recording averages of 4.1 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 1.6 assists.
